column2: smp: Trace smp callback causing an IPI

column1: Context
The newly-introduced ipi_send_cpumask tracepoint has a ""callback"" parameter
which so far has only been fed with NULL.
While CSD_TYPE_SYNC/ASYNC and CSD_TYPE_IRQ_WORK share a similar backing
struct layout (meaning their callback func can be accessed without caring
about the actual CSD type)
column2: CSD_TYPE_TTWU doesn't even have a function

column1: attached to its struct. This means we need to check the type of a CSD
before eventually dereferencing its associated callback.
This isn't as trivial as it sounds: the CSD type is stored in
__call_single_node.u_flags
column2: which get cleared right before the callback is

column1: executed via csd_unlock(). This implies checking the CSD type before it is
enqueued on the call_single_queue
column2: as the target CPU's queue can be flushed

column1: before we get to sending an IPI.
Furthermore
column2: send_call_function_single_ipi() only has a CPU parameter

column1: would need to have an additional argument to trickle down the invoked
function. This is somewhat silly
column2: as the extra argument will always be

column1: pushed down to the function even when nothing is being traced
unnecessary overhead.
Changes
send_call_function_single_ipi() is only used by smp.c
sched/core.c as it contains scheduler-specific ops (set_nr_if_polling() of
a CPU's idle task).
Split it into two parts: the scheduler bits remain in sched/core.c
actual IPI emission is moved into smp.c. This lets us define an
__always_inline helper function that can take the related callback as
parameter without creating useless register pressure in the non-traced path
which only gains a (disabled) static branch.
Do the same thing for the multi IPI case.
